newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan distorted truth on nuclear waste - Greepeace.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan distorted truth on nuclear waste - Greepeace.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace said on Wednesday that the nuclear waste Taiwan plans to ship to North Korea was "most dangerous" and that Taiwan's state utility had distorted the truth about contents of the barrels.
"Taiwan Power Company (Taipower) has seriously misrepresented the radioactivity of nuclear waste they plan to ship to North Korea," Greenpeace said in a statement.
"The waste is actually a soup of highly radioactive poisons, much more dangerous than claimed by the utility," it said.
A Taipower spokeswoman said the shipment would be safe.
"As we have always maintained, we would not have signed the deal to ship the waste to North Korea if we did not know the shipment is perfectly safe," Taipower spokeswoman Huang Huei-yu told Reuters."
The Taiwanese state utility signed a contract in January with Pyongyang to ship 200,000 barrels of low-radiation nuclear waste to North Korea.
The move immediately sparked protests from environmental groups and Pyongyang's long time rival, South Korea, which claimed the waste would pollute the Korean Peninsula.

"Greenpeace investigations reveal that Taipower has deliberately misrepresented the contents of the waste," the group's statement said. "The waste actually includes some of the most dangerous substances produced by nuclear reactors."
"Taipower's deception about the radioactivity of the waste calls into question their assurances that North Korea has the complex technology required to store it," it said.
Greenpeace said it would reveal the results of a study by the independent engineering group Large & Associates at a news conference at 3 p.m. (0700 GMT) in Hong Kong on Thursday.
Amid mounting criticism, Taiwan said in April it would press ahead with its plan to ship the waste to North Korea.
Taipower has said the waste would pose no health hazard and the shipment would not violate the regulations of the International Atomic Energy Agency.
